claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant Joseph J Orlan is linked at high confidence to the Joseph Orlan documented as an OSS communications officer killed in 1945.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary memorial supplies the exact name, lieutenant rank, OSS communications role, Signal Corps pathway, and wartime death chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the uncommon exact name, compatible lieutenant rank, direct OSS role, and coherent wartime chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The memorial was published in 1946 and describes service from 1940 through his death on 27 May 1945.
claims.match_notes: The article independently connects Joseph Orlan to OSS; it does not publish or repeat the private officer number.

sources.excerpt_override: Lt. Joseph Orlan ... a communications officer of the O.S.S.

claims.claim_text: By February 1936, Joseph J. Orlan described amateur radio as a hobby that had become his vocation.
claims.evidence_excerpt: my hobby (which, incidentally, has become my vocation)
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A signed contemporary contribution by Joseph J. Orlan says amateur radio had become his vocation.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Medium claim confidence within a high-confidence identity: exact name and compatible radio expertise, but no private identifier appears in the 1936 item.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly documented on 15 February 1936, before the United States entered World War II; not shown to be his immediate pre-OSS occupation.
claims.match_notes: Published as an occupation only. No employer, job title, start date, or immediate temporal relationship is inferred.

claims.claim_text: Joseph Orlan volunteered for service in 1940 and was assigned to the United States Army Signal Corps at Pearl Harbor.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Lt. Orlan entered service as a volunteer in 1940 and was assigned to the Signal Corps at Pearl Harbor.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The 1946 memorial describes Orlan's 1940 enlistment and Signal Corps assignment before recounting his later OSS communications work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the same contemporary account that names his OSS role and wartime death.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented as beginning in 1940, before OSS was established; the source does not state that Signal Corps was his immediate predecessor assignment.
claims.match_notes: Military assignment, not civilian employment. Immediate-pre-OSS status remains unproven.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Technician Fifth Grade Alekos X Orkoulas is the same person listed in a declassified OSS roster.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The index and declassified roster agree on the rare exact name, grade, and protected identifier.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact name, exact grade, and a matching protected identifier in two official RG 226 records.
claims.temporal_assessment: The roster is a wartime OSS record and supplies identity context, not a pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: The index note 'also AS' is preserved without expansion. No postwar restaurant work is treated as pre-OSS evidence.

claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact name, grade, and protected identifier in the official index and a contemporary OSS order.
claims.temporal_assessment: The order documents an OSS assignment on 9 May 1945; it does not identify pre-OSS employment.
claims.match_notes: The order is used for identity and OSS assignment context only.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Technician Fifth Grade Peter C Orlich is linked at high confidence to the radio operator on the OSS Weihsien rescue mission.
claims.evidence_excerpt: T/5 Peter C. Orlich, radio operator
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A direct-witness historical compilation gives the exact name, grade, and radio-operator role on the mission.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from exact uncommon name, exact technician grade, and specific OSS mission role.
claims.temporal_assessment: The material documents wartime OSS service and recalls that he worked before college, but it names no pre-OSS employer or occupation.
claims.match_notes: A Columbia scholarship and a family need for him to work are not converted into student status or an unnamed employer claim.
